title: How do these four fractions look as decimals?
description: Two over five, thirteen over four, four over fifty and five over eight are each given a bottom of ten, a hundred or a thousand. The top is multiplied by the same number as the bottom, and the result is read as a decimal. A check multiplies one answer back.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose the number that makes each bottom ten, a hundred or a thousand, and multiply the top and the bottom by it. Watch for students who write four fiftieths as zero point eight, forgetting that a hundred below gives hundredths.

video_script.why: The child has turned quarters into hundredths but not chosen the multiplier for each bottom.
video_script.substitution: Each bottom is turned into ten, a hundred or a thousand by multiplying top and bottom alike.
video_script.anchor: Two fifths, thirteen quarters, four fiftieths and five eighths
video_script.payoff_line: Five eighths is zero point six two five.

final_answer.spoken: zero point four, three point two five, zero point zero eight and zero point six two five

video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 2/5 is read two over five, 13/4 is thirteen over four, 4/50 is four over fifty, 5/8 is five over eight, and 625/1000 is six hundred and twenty five over a thousand.
video_script.design: The four fractions stay on the board; each line of the solution turns one bottom into ten, a hundred or a thousand.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four fractions side by side: 2/5, 13/4, 4/50, 5/8, each with an empty decimal box

marks.fracs: the four fractions appear one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about writing fractions as decimals.
<bookmark mark='fracs'/>The fractions are two over five, thirteen over four, four over fifty and five over eight.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are these four fractions as decimals?

beats.on_screen: the four fractions and their empty boxes stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Bottoms 5, 4, 50 and 8 are matched to 10, 100 and 1000; multiply top and bottom by the same number

marks.same: an arrow links the bottoms to ten, a hundred or a thousand
marks.rule: the words top and bottom, same number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. First make each bottom ten, a hundred or a thousand.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number, so the fraction stays equal.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four fractions. Two over five, thirteen over four, four over fifty and five over eight.

beats.on_screen: To find: each fraction as a decimal

marks.find: the four decimal boxes are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each fraction as a decimal.
<bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, two over five, where five times two is ten.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by two. We get four over ten.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Four over ten is four tenths, which is zero point four.
<bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, thirteen over four, where four times twenty five is a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by twenty five. Thirteen times twenty five is three hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Three hundred and twenty five over a hundred is three point two five.
<bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, four over fifty, where fifty times two is a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by two. We get eight over a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>Eight over a hundred is eight hundredths, which is zero point zero eight.

marks.s4c: 625/1000 is written with the decimal left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, five over eight, where eight times a hundred and twenty five is a thousand.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by a hundred and twenty five. Five times a hundred and twenty five is six hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>We get six hundred and twenty five over a thousand.

marks.s5b: the product 13 is matched with the top of 13/4

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, check by putting an answer back. Three point two five times four is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>That matches the top of the fraction thirteen over four.

marks.rest: the other three decimals are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five eighths is zero point six two five.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other three are zero point four, three point two five and zero point zero eight.
